title: Conormal stabilization gives equations on principal smooth opens
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B$ a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ an open subscheme smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There exist a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra $D$, $R$-algebra maps $i:B\to D$ and $r:D\to B$ with $ri=\mathrm{id}_B$, integers $N\geq c\geq0$, and a surjection $p:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]\twoheadrightarrow D$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with kernel $J$, having the following property. Put $W_D=(\operatorname{Spec}i)^{-1}(W)$. For every $h\in P$ such that $D_D(p(h))\subseteq W_D$, there exist $s\in P$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in J$ such that $D_D(p(s))=D_D(p(h))$, $sJ\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ in $P$, and the images of the $c\times c$ minors of $(\partial f_j/\partial x_k)_{1\leq j\leq c,1\leq k\leq N}$ generate the unit ideal of $D[1/p(s)]$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Here $D_D(a)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}D:a\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $D[1/a]$ inverts the powers of $a$. For $c=0$ the sole minor is $1$.

source.place: Elkik II, Lemma 3, printed pp.562–564, and the ambient-neighbourhood equations reduction in the proof of Lemma 4, pp.564–565; read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED. No exact Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text: Choose a presentation $B=P_0/I$, $P_0=R[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$, $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, and put $M=I/I^2$. Set $D=\operatorname{Sym}_B(M)$, $N=n+m$, $c=m$. The symmetric algebra universal property gives the structure map $i:B\to D$ and the augmentation $r:D\to B$ induced by $M\to B$, $u\mapsto0$; $ri=1$. The classes of $g_j$ generate $M$, so the symmetric-algebra generation theorem gives the surjection $p:P=P_0[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\twoheadrightarrow D$ with $p(y_j)=\iota([g_j])$. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem makes $P_0$ and $P$ Noetherian; $D$, being finite type over $R$, is finitely presented over $R$ by the Noetherian finite-presentation theorem. This single $p$ and $c\leq N$ are fixed before any principal open is chosen.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, lines 357–437; Elkik II Lemma 3, pp.562–564, and Lemma 4 proof p.565 (online scan; archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: The presentation-improvement theorem applies to this same $D=\operatorname{Sym}_B(I/I^2)$: for each $a\in B$ with $B_a$ smooth over $R$, $D_{i(a)}$ is smooth over $R$. Since $W$ is smooth, for a principal open $D_B(a)\subseteq W$ the open-immersion theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the inclusion of $D_B(a)$, restriction to opens and invariance under isomorphism make $\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth, and the affine smooth-morphism/smooth-ring-map comparison makes $B_a$ a smooth $R$-algebra. Conversely each $D_{i(a)}$ given by the presentation-improvement theorem is a smooth ring map, so $\operatorname{Spec}D_{i(a)}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth by the same comparison, and $D_D(i(a))\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth by the open-immersion theorem and restriction (b),(c). They cover $W$. Their inverse images cover $W_D$, so smoothness local on the source shows that $W_D\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth. Moreover on each such $B_a$, the split conormal differential sequence exhibits $M_a$ as a summand of $B_a^{\oplus n}$. It is finite projective; the finite-projective local-freeness theorem makes $M_{\mathfrak p}$ finite free for every $\mathfrak p\in W$.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, lines 357–437; Elkik II Lemma 3, pp.562–564, and Lemma 4 proof p.565 (online scan; archival copy WANTED).

proof.text:
Fix $h\in P$ and put $a=p(h)$ and $T=D[1/a]$, assuming $D_D(a)\subseteq W_D$. Every prime of $T$ contracts to a point of $W$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so Step 2 verifies exactly the free-locus hypothesis of the symmetric-conormal exact-sequence lemma (applied with base ring $P_0$, ideal $I$, and symmetric-algebra element $a$). Its two split sequences give
$$(J/J^2)\otimes_D T\cong(M\otimes_B T)\oplus(K\otimes_B T)\cong T^{\oplus m}.$$
If $T=0$, take $s=0$ and all $f_j=0$: the open is empty, $sJ=0$, and every ideal in the zero localization is the unit ideal. Henceforth $T\ne0$. Choose a basis of this localized conormal. Each basis element is a fraction represented by an element of $J$ with denominator a power of $h$. Clear denominators separately; this rescales basis vectors by units of $T$ and gives $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in J$ whose conormal classes are a $T$-basis.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, lines 357–437; Elkik II Lemma 3, pp.562–564, and Lemma 4 proof p.565 (online scan; archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: Write $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\subseteq P$ and $A'=P[1/h]$. The basis spans the localized conormal, so $J A'=F A'+(J A')^2$: for any $j/h^v$, express its class as a linear combination of the $f_j$ modulo $(J A')^2$ and lift those coefficients from $T=A'/J A'$ to $A'$. Thus the finite $A'$-module $E=J A'/F A'$ satisfies $(J A')E=E$. The one-plus-ideal form of Nakayama gives $e\in1+J A'$ with $eE=0$. Write $e=u/h^b$ with $u\in P$, $b\geq0$. Then $uJ A'\subseteq F A'$ and the image of $u/h^b$ in $T$ is $1$. Consequently $p(u)$ is a unit on $D_D(a)$ and $D_D(p(hu))=D_D(a)$.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, lines 357–437; Elkik II Lemma 3, pp.562–564, and Lemma 4 proof p.565 (online scan; archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: The ideal $J$ is finitely generated because $P$ is Noetherian. Choose generators $v_1,\ldots,v_t$. From $uv_l/1\in F P[1/h]$, the defining equality of fractions gives some $b_l\geq0$ with $h^{b_l}uv_l\in F$. Choose $b\geq b_l$ for all $l$ (take $b=0$ if $t=0$), and then $k\geq\max(1,b)$. Set $s=(hu)^k$. For every generator $v_l$, $sv_l=h^{k-b}u^{k-1}(h^buv_l)\in F$, proving $sJ\subseteq F$. An element is outside a prime exactly when each positive-power factor is, so $D_D(p(s))=D_D(p(hu))=D_D(a)$.

source.place: Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation), proof, lines 357–437; Elkik II Lemma 3, pp.562–564, and Lemma 4 proof p.565 (online scan; archival copy WANTED).

proof.text: The open $D_D(a)\subseteq W_D$, identified with $\operatorname{Spec}T$ by the open-immersion theorem, is smooth over $R$ by Step 2 and restriction to opens; the affine smooth-morphism/smooth-ring-map comparison makes $T$ a smooth $R$-algebra, as the split conormal theorem requires. Apply the split conormal differential theorem to the fixed polynomial presentation $p$ localized at $a$. In the basis $[f_1],\ldots,[f_c]$ of Step 3, its injection into $T^{\oplus N}$ is the Jacobian matrix with entries $\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_k}$. A left inverse therefore supplies matrices $A$ of size $c\times N$ (this Jacobian) and $L$ of size $N\times c$ with $AL=1_c$. Cauchy–Binet gives $1=\det(AL)=\sum_{|S|=c}\det(A^S)\det(L_S)$, so the $c\times c$ Jacobian minors generate the unit ideal of $T$. Since $D_D(p(s))=D_D(a)$, each of $p(s)$ and $a$ is a unit after inverting the other; the universal properties identify $D[1/p(s)]$ with $T$. The same minor identity holds there. For $c=0$ it is the empty determinant identity $1=1$.
